ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, to estimate the width of the fish pond $AB$, Xiao Kai took points $C$, $D$, and $E$ on the land such that $A$, $C$, $D$ are on the same straight line and $B$, $C$, $E$ are on the same straight line. It was measured that $CD = \frac{1}{2}AC$ and $CE = \frac{1}{2}BC$. Xiao Kai measured the length of $DE$ to be 10 meters. What is the length of the fish pond width $AB$ in meters?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $CD=\frac{1}{2}AC, CE=\frac{1}{2}BC$,\\
it follows that $\frac{CD}{AC}=\frac{CE}{BC}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
and since $\angle DCE=\angle ACB$,\\
it implies $\triangle DCE\sim \triangle ACB$,\\
hence $\frac{ED}{AB}=\frac{CD}{AC}=\frac{1}{2}$.\\
Given $ED=10\text{m}$,\\
therefore $AB=\boxed{20\text{m}}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the upper part of the figure is the fish pond width AB, A is at the upper left, B is at the upper right; two oblique lines intersect at C, among which A, C, D are on the same straight line, and B, C, E are on the same straight line; below there is line segment ED, and the figure forms the upper large triangle ACB and the lower small triangle DCE. Reasoning: It is known that CD = 1/2 AC, CE = 1/2 BC, so CD/AC = CE/BC = 1/2. Because A, C, D are collinear and B, C, E are collinear, ∠DCE and ∠ACB are vertical angles and are equal. Therefore triangle DCE and triangle ACB are similar by SAS. The corresponding sides satisfy DE/AB = CD/AC = 1/2. Also DE = 10 meters, so AB = 2 × 10 = 20 meters.
